## In one sentence

Evaluation estimates how well a model will perform on the data and decisions
that matter after training.

## Splitting data

Use training data to fit models, validation data to choose among approaches, and
an untouched test set for final assessment. Cross-validation repeatedly rotates
training and validation folds when data are limited. Time-ordered or grouped
data require splits that respect their structure.

## Metrics

For classification, accuracy can hide class imbalance; precision, recall,
ROC-AUC, and calibration answer different questions. For regression, mean
absolute error is in outcome units, while squared-error metrics emphasise large
mistakes. Choose a metric before comparing models.

::: {.callout-important}
Never tune a model on the final test set. Repeatedly checking it turns the test
set into training information and makes performance look too optimistic.
:::

## Check your understanding

Choose a metric for a rare-disease screening model and explain the costs of false
positives and false negatives.
